title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 275 (Company liquidators and their appointments)

content.overview: For the winding up of a company the Tribunal appoints an official liquidator or a company liquidator from the panel maintained under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, as the section provides.
content.glance: For the winding up of a company the Tribunal appoints an official liquidator or a company liquidator from the panel maintained under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, as the section provides.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 275 (Company liquidators and their appointments). For the winding up of a company the Tribunal appoints an official liquidator or a company liquidator from the panel maintained under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, as the section provides. Apply only the conditions, approvals, filings and penalties stated in the section. A rule made under the Act cannot contradict the section. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: For the winding up of a company the Tribunal appoints an official liquidator or a company liquidator from the panel maintained under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, as the section provides.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: The liquidator is an insolvency professional in the current scheme. The appointment terms include remuneration. The old company-paid liquidator panel has been aligned with the Code.
